why: Look at the L-shaped line figures. Every figure has a flat base line and one stick joined to it. In the series the stick moves along the base (left end, middle, then right end) and also tilts, so the figures keep changing and never repeat. After the stick has stood straight at the right end in figure 4, the next step tilts it over the base from the right end, which gives option 4. Options 1, 2, 3 and 5 are just copies of figures already shown in the series (L, tilted left, upside-down T, and the right-end corner), so they do not continue the pattern.
trick: Track how the stick joins the base (which end, which angle) in each figure. The answer is usually the one new position, not a copy of an earlier figure.
note: Ambiguous: the rule is hard to pin down. Options 1,2,3,5 repeat earlier figures, so option 4 is chosen by elimination as the only new figure.
